claims.claim: ⚠️ **Even when treated, meningococcal disease can kill rapidly.** Mortality is up to 10% despite prompt treatment; 10–20% are left with long-term morbidity such as deafness, amputations or neurological deficits.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **It presents as sepsis with DIC and a fast-spreading petechial/purpuric rash that does not blanch** (higher mortality), **or as meningitis, with or without a rash**; less often as septic arthritis, pneumonia, pharyngitis, conjunctivitis or occult bacteraemia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **History:** over <12 hours, headache, nausea, vomiting, poor appetite, sore throat and coryza come on quickly; fever; myalgia or leg pain. **Infants may show only poor feeding, irritability, lethargy, mottling or a high-pitched moaning cry.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examination:** cool peripheries and/or pallor or mottling · altered conscious state · headache, neck stiffness, photophobia, bulging fontanelle · **non-blanching petechiae/purpura**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A blanching rash does not exclude it**; the rash can initially be macular or maculopapular and blanch.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Risk factors:** being Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander; immunodeficiency (asplenia, immunoglobulin or complement deficiency, sickle cell disease, HSCT, HIV); cigarette smoke; crowded housing; prolonged contact with a carrier. **Ask about vaccination status, including MenB.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Investigations must not delay antibiotics.** Blood (IV or intraosseous) for culture before antibiotics if possible, plus PCR in a separate EDTA tube.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CSF only once stabilised and with no contraindication to LP:** cell count, biochemistry, Gram stain (Gram-negative diplococci), culture ± meningococcal PCR.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Until meningococcal infection is confirmed, treat and resuscitate as for sepsis.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **The moment meningococcal disease is suspected, give ceftriaxone/cefotaxime — within 15 minutes**; if neither is available, give benzylpenicillin. Empiric treatment is a third-generation cephalosporin.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Beyond 4 weeks of life: IV ceftriaxone once daily, 100 mg/kg (max 4 g).**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Alternatively IV cefotaxime, 50 mg/kg (max 2 g)** — 12-hourly in week 1 of life, 6–8-hourly in weeks 2–4, 6-hourly after week 4.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No IV or intraosseous access: give it IM** — volume or muscle size may mean two injections — then give the dose again when IV access is obtained.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No ceftriaxone/cefotaxime available? IV benzylpenicillin, 60 mg/kg (max 2.4 g)** — 12-hourly in week 1, 6-hourly in weeks 2–4, 4-hourly after week 4.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Children treated with benzylpenicillin also need contact-prophylaxis antibiotics** to eradicate carriage.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Anticipate rapid deterioration.** Carefully titrated fluid resuscitation with repeated assessment, and **early consideration of inotropes**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Confirmed disease: 5 days of IV treatment.** Continue the third-generation cephalosporin until sensitivities are confirmed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Once benzylpenicillin susceptibility is confirmed, de-escalate to it**: IV, 60 mg/kg (max 2.4 g) — 12-hourly in week 1, 6-hourly in weeks 2–4, 4-hourly after week 4.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Dexamethasone given for empiric meningitis can be stopped once N. meningitidis is confirmed** — no clearly demonstrated benefit.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Isolate with droplet precautions** per local infection-control guidelines.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Notify every presumed or confirmed case immediately** to the local state authority.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Give contact prophylaxis to at-risk contacts as soon as possible.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cases:** vaccinate only if the case has underlying risk factors. **Contacts:** for serogroups A, C, W or Y, non-immunised contacts may be offered vaccination as secondary prevention; **a single first dose of MenB is unlikely to protect a contact during the risk period.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Manage every child with acute meningococcal disease in a facility that can provide intensive care**; if unavailable, stabilise and transfer. Consult the local paediatric team for all suspected cases.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge:** IV treatment can be completed through HITH once haemodynamically stable and afebrile, and after contact prophylaxis has been considered.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Acute meningococcal disease' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Acute_meningococcal_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23
